title: docs(adr): ADR-0162 closed states on an object close the record and its lines
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu2JFaDAE2Vf69revbwwFEXe)_

Part of #36253. This PR is the card's "ADR first" half. The build half stays on the card and starts only after this record is accepted.

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户无感：这次只落一份设计记录，线上行为不变；记录获批并实现后，业务人员会看到已付款、已审批通过这类已关闭的单据连同它的明细行，在任何入口都不能再手工修改或删除。
- 为什么做：属于「单据关闭后锁定」这项功能，替需要把已决单据冻结的应用解决问题，今天这些应用只能各自手写代码去拦。
- 出错会怎样：这份记录本身不影响任何人；其中的选择如果不合适，批准前直接改文字，批准后再出一份修订记录，没有数据需要回滚。
- 要你做什么：审批这份设计记录；你 11 月 26 日的两次裁定（「全部按推荐」和「平台堵住：撤回不恢复关闭值」）已经写进正文，增量审核通过后请批准合并。

## What changes

- Adds `docs/adr/0162-an-object-declares-its-closed-states-the-record-and-its-lines-are-closed-to-change.md`, status **Proposed**.
- Regenerates `docs/adr/README.md` with `scripts/adr-index.mjs` (one new row, three counts).
- No code, no schema key, no route, no changeset. The record declares; it implements nothing.

What the record decides, in the order the card asks:

| Card asks | Record answers |
|---|---|
| The key's shape | D1, D2: an object-level `closedStates` map from a state field to the values that close a record. Nothing is stored for it; closed is read off the stored row. |
| The unit | D3: the record and its direct `master_detail` lines, the unit the pending-approval lock holds. |
| Exemptions, and delete | D4 to D7: every caller is bound at every door, the state field included, and no grant lifts it. A write that names no principal is bound too. A system context is not bound. A caller cannot delete a closed record, and a delete whose cascade would reach one is refused whole before anything is removed. Referential clears, restore and a change of owner are named case by case. A new approval round stays a way out of a state closed on the approval's status field, and an abandoned round never writes a closed value. |
| One lock read | D8, D9: one refusal code, `RECORD_LOCKED`, with its own sentence. One read owned by the data layer answers for both producers, and tells every caller who can read the record whether it is locked and which lock holds. The approvals-family read stays exactly as published. |
| Where it is enforced | D10: in the engine's write path, after the object-permission and row-access gates and before the app's hooks. A many-row write is judged by one existence probe asked of the store. A line write asks the caller's own read door before it consults a master the write names. |

**Four points go past the ruling's words, and the maintainer has ruled on them.** The ruling of 2026-11-26 ([record](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/36253#issuecomment-7200732942), 「全部按推荐」, all as recommended) adopts each as the record writes it. Each stays marked in the text, with the other reading beside it in "Points the ruling does not settle":

1. D5: a system context is not bound at all, where the card's words require only a sanctioned action that moves the state. An action button's script is such a context, and works on a closed document as on an open one.
2. D6: a caller cannot delete a closed record, where a pending one can still be deleted.
3. D4: the lock is judged on the stored row only, so the write that closes a record lands whole. Item ③ of the 2026-11-22 batch governs `readonlyWhen` and not this lock.
4. D9: a new read owned by the data layer answers for both producers and names the reason. The approvals-family read stays as published and answers for approvals only; whether its routes retire or are redirected is a card filed with the build cards.

The same ruling settled three points the second contract review left open:

- **Who is told the lock's reason.** Every caller who can read the record. D9 states what that discloses to a reader whom field permissions keep from the state field, and why it is accepted.
- **A delete's cascade.** Judged whole, before the first row is removed. The refusal names the record the caller asked to delete and the label of the object in the way, and nothing of the closed record itself. D6 states the exception this makes.
- **A new approval round.** It stays a way out of a closed state. D5 names each outcome and where the author gates it.

**A second ruling the same day** ([record](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/36253#issuecomment-7201405662), 「平台堵住：撤回不恢复关闭值」, the platform blocks it: a recall does not restore a closed value) answers the point the third contract review raised. The new approval round stays a way out, and D5 gains one platform rule. When a request is abandoned, by its submitter's recall, by an administrator's override or by the sweep of a dead run, the approval status mirror never writes a value the object declares closed, `recalled` included. The approvals-plugin change is a build card (Execution, item 7), released with the key.

## Small decisions

The second ruling leaves the thread to say what the mirror writes in place of a closed value. Three choices are the thread's, and the fourth is the seat's reading. Each is stated in D5 and listed in "Points the ruling does not settle", with the ones not taken in Alternatives, "What an abandoned round writes":

1. **What is written instead.** The value a record that was never submitted carries: the field's declared default, or empty where the default is a closed value or there is none. The field does not go on reading `pending` with no request open.
2. **A record the round never moved is left alone.** Where the field still holds the value it held at submit and that value is a closed one, the mirror writes nothing. Without this, a round opened and recalled on a field that declares neither `pending` nor `returned` would take the approval away from a document nobody could touch. A record the round left on a closed `pending` or `returned` is not left there: it goes down the same order as any other.
3. **Released with the key.** The key is not published while an abandoned round can still write a closed value.
4. **A `recalled` the object closes on is not written either** (the seat's reading, by the text of the option the maintainer chose, on [record](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/36253#issuecomment-7202242844)). The field is then treated as one that declares no `recalled` value. The maintainer's own word is 恢复, restore, and the narrower reading, a rule on the put-back only, is in Alternatives.

One cost follows from the ruling and is stated in Consequences: a round started by mistake on a decided document and then recalled leaves the document open, and it has to be approved again.

**Read first**, by risk:

1. D5, "An abandoned round never writes a closed value", with its group in Alternatives considered.
2. D9, "Every reader of the record is told `locked`" and "What that discloses, and why it is accepted".
3. D6, "Cascades": what is judged, when, what the refusal names, and the exception.
4. D10, "A line write reaches a master in one of two ways", with the last group in Alternatives considered.
5. D5, the other outcomes of an approval round, and which actions run elevated.

**Revised after the contract review of the first head** ([review](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/37606#issuecomment-7196241005), PASS with six points to fix and six nits). Every point is answered in the record's own text:

| Review point | Where it is answered |
|---|---|
| A many-row write should be probed in the store, not listed | D4, "Asked of the store, not listed" and "What cannot be judged is refused" |
| Item ③ was restated with a word the ruling does not carry | Header, D4's last paragraph, the third marked point, Alternatives |
| The showcase changes in more than two outcomes | Execution item 3, "What it costs" |
| `lockSource` has a published delete reading | D9: the delete reading holds only under an approval; the approvals-family read is left as published |
| Three kinds of writer, not two | D5, "The test" |
| The approval mirror moves a record out of a closed value | D5 and "What an author has to know" |
| The six nits | D8 (the upload-link door's own sentence; the refusal names no producer), D9 (two readability anchors), the Context table and D5 (the pending lock's other two passes), "What an author has to know" (create with lines), Readings (the unresolved case) |

**Revised after the delta review of `fe9a850c`** ([review](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/37606#issuecomment-7197474873), PASS with two points to fix and three nits) **and the ruling**:

| Review point | Where it is answered |
|---|---|
| D8 and D9 said the reason rule achieves more than the rest of D9 lets it | D9: the rule is gone; every reader is told the reason, and the disclosure is stated. D8 loses its sentence about the read. Alternatives keep both readings not taken. |
| D10's sentence was categorical, and the cascade was a case it did not cover | D10: the promise is scoped to the object-permission and row-access gates. D6: the cascade's judgement, its refusal and its exception. D8: the cascade's own sentence. |
| The per-row ceiling was misdescribed and misanchored | D4 and Readings |
| The upload-link door's sentence for a caller given no reason | D8: the door chooses its sentence by the read's reason, which a locked answer always carries |
| No alternative was recorded for the approval-round path | Alternatives, "A request is not opened on a closed record"; D5 |
| A line write and a master its writer cannot read | D10's two rules; D4, "One refusal is another gate's"; Alternatives |
| Where field permissions are asked | D10: in the security layer's middleware, ahead of the engine's hooks |
| What a change of owner does on a closed record | D7, "What an author has to know", the left-open list |

**Revised after the delta review of `f79eda94`** ([review](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/37606#issuecomment-7201298747), PASS with one point to fix and six nits) **and the second ruling**:

| Review point | Where it is answered |
|---|---|
| D5 and the author note said the state field always tells what happened | D5: each outcome is stated by the values the field declares, and the rule on an abandoned round follows. Consequences and Alternatives match. |
| The pending lock holds a pending round only where the approval node locks | D5, "While the request is pending" |
| Two writers that abandon a request were not named | D5, "Abandoned"; Readings |
| The cascade's sentence did not fit the second case D6 judges, nor say when it takes the label form | D8 |
| What a line's reader is told | D9, "What that discloses, and why it is accepted" |
| The ruling was quoted in English | Header: both rulings verbatim, with an English reading beside each |
| Three nits the review routes to the build cards: the `lockSource` member under an approval, a master that a hook supplies, an action's registered handler | Not changed here. They go to the build cards with the review record. |
| The ruling record's own wording | No change in this PR |

**Revised after the delta review of `eec0a5e1`** ([review](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/37606#issuecomment-7202211190), PASS with one point to fix and seven nits):

| Review point | Where it is answered |
|---|---|
| The "left alone" test stranded a record on an in-flight status the object closes on | D5: the mirror writes nothing only where the field still holds its value at submit; a field the round left on a closed `pending` or `returned` goes down the order. The author's note, Execution item 7's test list and Alternatives name the case. D5 also states the one corner the rule does not reach, a required field with no usable default, and hands it to the approvals card. |
| Two sentences on an abandoned round were true only of a round that opened the document | Consequences, both entries |
| A third thing inside the second ruling is the record's own, and "to the letter" was the wrong name for it | Header, D5, "Points the ruling does not settle", Alternatives: it is the seat's reading of the chosen option's text |
| The second ruling's time | Header: recorded at 19:16Z |
| "A stacked pair" in Execution item 1 | A trunk branch, as `AGENTS.md` has it |
| Three nits the review routes to the approvals card: the validator on a readonly field, the override arm admitting a system context, a log line when a value is withheld | Not changed here |

## Tests

None. The diff is two Markdown files under `docs/adr/`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Tier H.** `docs/adr/**` is a governed surface. This PR stays a draft: it is not merged, queued, armed or marked ready by its author. It lands by the maintainer's merge or an authorized approval.
- **L2.** The contract-tier review of the first head and the delta reviews of `fe9a850c`, `f79eda94` and `eec0a5e1` passed. This head answers the fourth review's point and four of its nits. It owes one more delta review. The seat runs it. This thread does not review its own record.
- **Premise.** Checked on `main` at `6c290d3af7` and it holds: the approvals guide still says "the record unlocks", the showcase still carries the three paid-invoice hooks, no key of this meaning exists on the object schema, and the pending line lock is on `main`. One item was not checked: the card names a hosted app's edit guards as a producer. That app's code is outside this repository; the record relies on it only as the card states it.
- **`skip-changeset`.** `docs/adr/**` publishes nothing from any released package.
- **Readings the record states but did not run.** Four, listed under "Execution" for the build to verify and pin: the order of the approval status mirror and the request's finalisation, which engine-derived writes reach a closed record and in which context, whether a customization overlay may add or shorten the declaration, and what the mirror's put-back does when it comes down to an empty value on a required field.
- **Deviation.** In the first round one gate needed two packages built first, and that build ran without the shared verify lock. No build ran in this round.
